Circumcise
SUR-kum-size
v.
From Latin circumcidere, “to cut around,” from circum (around) + caedere (to cut). Renders the Hebrew mūl, “to circumcise,” and the Greek peritemnō, “to cut around.”

📖 Biblical Definition

To circumcise is to apply the covenant sign given to Abraham and his seed—the cutting away of the foreskin of every male child of the household at the eighth day, the bloody token in the body of the everlasting covenant God made with Abraham and his seed after him. This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised... and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you. Circumcision is therefore not first a hygienic, ethnic, or cultural practice but a covenantal sign of belonging—the seal of the righteousness of the faith that Abraham had yet being uncircumcised, the mark of the people God claimed as His own, the bloody anticipation of a deeper cutting away that the prophets and apostles will identify as the circumcision of the heart. Moses commands it: circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked; Jeremiah pleads it: circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart; Paul completes it: he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; and again, in whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ. Under the New Covenant, physical circumcision has been fulfilled and superseded—the apostles fought a decisive battle at Jerusalem against the Judaizers who would have laid it upon Gentile believers as required for salvation; baptism has succeeded it as the covenant sign for the people of God; and what circumcision pointed to—the heart cut, the flesh put off, the soul covenantally claimed—is now wrought spiritually in every regenerate believer by the Spirit of God on the ground of the work of Christ. To miss this trajectory is to misread the whole flow of redemptive history; to follow it is to see, in the ancient bloody sign of Abraham’s seed, the gospel of the heart-circumcised people of God in Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines CIRCUMCISE as to cut off the prepuce or foreskin, according to the Jewish law; in a spiritual sense, to purify the heart from sinful affections.

expand to see more

CIRCUMCISE, v.t. — 1. To cut off the prepuce or foreskin of males, according to the Jewish law; a religious rite or ceremony, the token of the covenant between God and Abraham and his posterity (Gen 17). 2. In a spiritual sense, to purify the heart from sinful affections (Deut 10:16; Rom 2:29).

CIRCUMCISION, n. — The act of cutting off the prepuce or foreskin; a Jewish rite, the token of the covenant with Abraham. Spiritually, the putting away of the sins of the flesh by the regenerating work of the Spirit.

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 17:10-11 — "This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you."

Deuteronomy 10:16 — "Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked."

Romans 2:29 — "But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God."

Colossians 2:11 — "In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Circumcision is corrupted, on one side, by the reduction of the discussion to a purely medical-cosmetic debate that flattens the covenantal-theological dimension; and on the other, by the Judaizing error of every age that would re-impose the Old Covenant sign upon the New Covenant people of God, missing the redemptive-historical trajectory from sign to fulfillment.

expand to see more

The contemporary discussion of circumcision is almost wholly medical-cosmetic—debates over neonatal pain, parental consent, hygiene benefits, and cultural appropriation—with the covenantal-theological dimension that occupies the biblical text dropped almost entirely from view. The Christian who reads Scripture closely will not flatten the topic to such terms. Circumcision in the Bible is first and centrally a covenant sign—the bloody token of God’s claim on Abraham and his seed, the seal of the righteousness of faith, the anticipation of the deeper heart-circumcision wrought by the Spirit on the ground of Christ’s work. To read the biblical material as if it were principally about pediatric medicine is to miss the theological architecture of the Old Testament and the apostolic argument of Romans 2–4, Galatians, and Colossians 2.

The opposite corruption is the Judaizing error that would re-impose the Old Covenant sign upon the New Covenant people of God—the precise error the apostles confronted at the Jerusalem council in Acts 15 and which Paul fought to the death of his ministry in Galatians. Under the New Covenant, physical circumcision has been fulfilled and superseded by the spiritual circumcision of the heart wrought by the Spirit on the ground of Christ’s work and signified outwardly in baptism; to insist upon physical circumcision as required for salvation or covenant standing is to fall from grace and to declare that Christ has profited the believer nothing. Read the redemptive-historical arc properly: the sign was given to Abraham, kept by Israel under the Law, anticipated the heart-circumcision the prophets pleaded for, and is fulfilled at the cross—where the body of the sins of the flesh is put off by the circumcision of Christ for all who are united to Him by faith.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mūl (to circumcise) and Greek peritemnō (to cut around): a covenant sign in the flesh that anticipates the deeper circumcision of the heart, wrought by the Spirit on the ground of the cross.

expand to see more

Hebrew mūl (H4135) — to circumcise; both physical (Gen 17) and metaphorical (Deut 10:16, heart).

Greek peritemnō (G4059) — to cut around, circumcise; literal and figurative.

Greek peritomē (G4061) — circumcision (the noun); also of the spiritual circumcision in Col 2:11.

Greek akrobustia (G203) — uncircumcision, the foreskin; the contrast term in Romans 2–4.

Usage

"Circumcision is first a covenant sign—the bloody token of God’s claim on Abraham’s seed, anticipating the heart-circumcision the prophets pleaded for."

"Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked—Moses already names the deeper reality the sign pointed to."

"Under the New Covenant, physical circumcision is fulfilled and superseded by baptism and by the circumcision made without hands; to re-impose it upon Gentile believers is the Judaizing error Paul confronted to the end."
